# M13-S1: -O levels and CPU targets (SPEC T-105). Levels apply to Go and
# loGo/s packages under logos and plain go; go help build stays upstream.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# O0 passes -N -l to the compiler.
logos build -a -x -O=0 .
stderr '\-N \-l'

# No flag means O2 under logos: inline budget 120, make threshold 256,
# standard synthetic PGO.
logos build -a -x .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=120,variablemakethreshold=256,logossynthpgo=standard'

# O2 is explicit too.
logos build -a -x -O=2 .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=120,variablemakethreshold=256,logossynthpgo=standard'

# O3 raises the inline budget, adds the recursive-cycle budget and the
# variable-make threshold, turns on specialization and aggressive PGO.
logos build -a -x -O=3 .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=400,inlrecursivebudget=80,variablemakethreshold=4096,logosspecialize=1,logossynthpgo=aggressive'

# The same flags apply to a Go module under logos build and go build.
cd gomod
logos build -a -x -O=2 .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=120,variablemakethreshold=256,logossynthpgo=standard'
go build -a -x -O=2 .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=120,variablemakethreshold=256,logossynthpgo=standard'

# Plain go without -O keeps the upstream default O1: none of the logos
# debug flags appear.
go build -a -x .
! stderr 'inlbudget'
! stderr 'variablemakethreshold'
! stderr 'logossynthpgo'
! stderr 'logosspecialize'

# An invalid level fails under go with the accepted set.
! go build -O=4 .
stderr 'go build: invalid -O level "4" \(want 0, 1, 2, 3, s, z\)'
cd ..

# An invalid level fails under logos with the accepted set.
! logos build -O=4 .
stderr 'logos build: invalid -O level "4" \(want 0, 1, 2, 3, s, z\)'

# go help build carries no -O text.
go help build
! stdout ' -O[= ]'

# Os and Oz lower the inline budget and fold identical code in the
# linker: the compile line carries -d=inlbudget=15, the link line carries
# -logos.icf, and the folded program still runs.
logos build -a -x -O=s .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=15'
stderr 'link .*-logos\.icf'
! stderr 'logossynthpgo'
logos run -O=s .
stdout '^hello$'
logos build -a -x -O=z .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=15'
stderr 'link .*-logos\.icf'
logos run -O=z .
stdout '^hello$'

# Only Os and Oz fold: O2 leaves the link line alone.
logos build -a -x -O=2 .
! stderr '\-logos\.icf'

# Os and Oz fold the same way for a Go module under go build.
cd gomod
go build -a -x -O=s .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=15'
stderr 'link .*-logos\.icf'
cd ..

# The default level comes from logos.toml [build] opt_level.
cd o3
logos build -a -x .
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=400,inlrecursivebudget=80,variablemakethreshold=4096,logosspecialize=1,logossynthpgo=aggressive'
# An explicit -O overrides the file.
logos build -a -x -O=1 .
! stderr 'inlbudget'
cd ..

# Bare and unknown opt_level spellings fail with file and position.
cd bad3
! logos build .
stderr 'logos\.toml:5:13: opt_level must be one of O0, O1, O2, O3, Os, Oz'
cd ../badO4
! logos build .
stderr 'logos\.toml:5:13: opt_level must be one of O0, O1, O2, O3, Os, Oz'
cd ..

# File arguments ignore logos.toml: the invalid opt_level is never read
# and the logos default level applies.
cd bad3
logos build -a -x main.lgo
stderr '\-d=inlbudget=120,variablemakethreshold=256,logossynthpgo=standard'
cd ..

# target_cpu deterministic (the default) selects v3 unless set.
logos build -a -x .
stderr 'GOAMD64=.v3.'
env GOAMD64=v2
logos build -a -x .
stderr 'GOAMD64=.v2.'
env GOAMD64=

# The arm64 lane follows the same rule under cross-compilation.
env GOARCH=arm64
logos build -a -x .
stderr 'GOARM64=.v8\.2.'
env GOARM64=v8.1
logos build -a -x .
stderr 'GOARM64=.v8\.1.'
env GOARM64=
env GOARCH=

# baseline pins the oldest CPUs; native picks the host level.
cd baseline
logos build -a -x .
stderr 'GOAMD64=.v1.'
cd ../native
logos build -a -x .
stderr 'GOAMD64=.v[134].'
cd ..

# The levels change what the compiled code does, not only the flags the
# compiler receives: a frame-local make of variable size stays off the
# heap up to the level's stack buffer and takes the heap one byte past
# it. The expected size is written here beside each command and is never
# read back from the build under test, so an optimization that stops
# working fails the probe. src/runtime/logos_mode_gate.bash carries the
# same level and size pairs for the runtime tests.
cd stackbuf
env WANT_STACKBUF=32
go test -count=1 .
stdout '^ok'
go test -count=1 -O=1 .
stdout '^ok'
logos test -count=1 -O=1 .
stdout '^ok'
env WANT_STACKBUF=256
go test -count=1 -O=2 .
stdout '^ok'
logos test -count=1 .
stdout '^ok'
logos test -count=1 -O=2 .
stdout '^ok'
env WANT_STACKBUF=4096
go test -count=1 -O=3 .
stdout '^ok'
logos test -count=1 -O=3 .
stdout '^ok'

# An explicit -gcflags pin still wins over the level's buffer.
env WANT_STACKBUF=32
go test -count=1 -O=3 -gcflags=all=-d=variablemakethreshold=32 .
stdout '^ok'

# A build whose buffer is not the expected one fails the probe: a level
# that lost its optimization cannot pass as a level that kept it.
env WANT_STACKBUF=4096
! go test -count=1 -O=3 -gcflags=all=-d=variablemakethreshold=32 .
stdout 'FAIL'
env WANT_STACKBUF=256
! go test -count=1 .
stdout 'FAIL'
env WANT_STACKBUF=
cd ..

-- stackbuf/go.mod --
module example.com/optlevels/stackbuf

go 1.27

-- stackbuf/stackbuf.go --
package stackbuf

-- stackbuf/stackbuf_test.go --
package stackbuf

import (
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"testing"
)

// probe is a frame-local make of variable size. The compiler keeps it in
// the frame when n is at most the stack buffer of the build.
//
//go:noinline
func probe(n int) byte {
	b := make([]byte, n)
	b[0] = 1
	return b[n-1]
}

func allocs(n int) float64 {
	return testing.AllocsPerRun(10, func() { _ = probe(n) })
}

func TestCompiledStackBuffer(t *testing.T) {
	want, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Getenv("WANT_STACKBUF"))
	if err != nil || want < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("WANT_STACKBUF=%q: want a byte count of at least 2", os.Getenv("WANT_STACKBUF"))
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		n     int
		stack bool
	}{
		{want / 2, true},
		{want, true},
		{want + 1, false},
		{2*want + 1, false},
	} {
		if got := allocs(c.n); (got == 0) != c.stack {
			t.Errorf("make of %d bytes took %v allocations, want the stack buffer of %d bytes to decide: stack=%v", c.n, got, want, c.stack)
		}
	}
}
